subject: Degrees of freedom in scalar invariance model

messages.author: f2b4ea1ef2b51d80
messages.subject: Degrees of freedom in scalar invariance model
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am testing for the invariance of a scale and trying to work out what the degrees of freedom from a series of nested multi-group (two groups) models represent. I have a psychological self-report scale including tot. 25 items, loading onto three correlated latent variables. In particular, I have a doubt about the step of scalar invariance. My code:

fit_scalar <- cfa(baseline,
                  sample.cov = list(Control = control, Clìnical = clinical),
                  sample.mean = list(Control = control_means, Clìnical = clinical_means),
                  sample.nobs = c(control_n, clinical_n),
                  group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))

The output reports 159 model parameters and 47 equality constraints, for total 588 degrees of freedom. My attempt, based on lavaan's output:

Observed variables                25
Total sample moments                350
Latent variances                3
Latent residual variances        0
Latent covariances                3
Latent means                        0 in one group, 3 in the other group
Measurement loadings                22
Measurement intercepts                25
Measurement residuals                25
       
Total sample moments                700
Total to be estimated                159
Total constrained                47
Degrees of freedom                588

I would be grateful for any help to understand if the model I am running and my interpretation are correct.

Thank you

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Degrees of freedom in scalar invariance model
parts:
The numbers seem right.  Remember to multiply the number of unconstrained estimates (latent (co)variances and residuals) by 2 because there are that many per group.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
